Points: On Nov 22, the U.S. began reviewing restrictions on NVIDIA’s H200 AI chip exports to China — a move signaling a cautious thaw in tech relations despite ongoing strategic competition. | On Nov 25, Donald Trump said Xi Jinping agreed to accelerate purchases of U.S. goods following a “positive, friendly and constructive” call between the two leaders. China’s Foreign Ministry said the communication was crucial for developing stable US-China relations. | It is revealed that Donald Trump may visit Shenzhen for the 2026 APEC, The U.S. Treasury Secretary stressed that frequent leader-level engagement would bring “stability” to bilateral relations and global markets, even as both sides remain strategic rivals.

Topic: China Opens Draft Regulations on Data Protection to Public Consultation
Points: On Nov 22, China’s Cyberspace Administration and Ministry of Public Security released a draft regulation aimed at tightening personal information protection on large online platforms. Public consultation on the draft regulations is open until Dec 22. | Key provisions include: Data Localization: All personal data collected in China must be stored domestically; overseas transfers require compliance with national security rules. | User Rights: Platforms must provide easy channels for users to access, correct, delete data, and close accounts. | Security Measures: Encourages use of national identity authentication, data labeling, and certification to enhance protection.

Topic: Chinese VP urges manufacturing upgrades trade diversification in policy push
Points: Concluding a three-day inspection in Hubei and Hunan, Chinese vice-premier He Lifeng called for accelerating technological innovation, strengthening manufacturing, and diversifying export markets to sustain growth amid global uncertainties. | He emphasized removing barriers to a unified domestic market, supporting cross-border e-commerce and overseas warehouses, and building modern logistics systems to cut costs, aligning with China’s broader push for high-quality, innovation-driven development.

Topic: Ancient Egypt Exhibition Overwhelmed by Visitors
Points: The Ancient Egyptian Civilization Exhibition held at the Hong Kong Palace Museum, saw record crowds on Nov 22, with wait times reaching 90 minutes. | Merchandise sales soared — 50 times higher than usual, with the blind boxes (The Pharaoh's Cat Plush Series) got sold out within two days. The following pictures shows some of the plush, which are slightly larger than a hand.

Topic: CPC 20th Central Committee’s Fourth Plenary Session Seminar Held
Points: The HKSAR Government hosted seminars on the spirit of the CPC 20th Central Committee’s Fourth Plenary Session (四中全會) featuring central delegates Hou Jianguo and Zhu Weidong. The briefing outlined priorities for the upcoming 15th Five-Year Plan, including high-quality development, technological self-reliance, and deeper integration into national strategies such as the Greater Bay Area. | John Lee stressed aligning Hong Kong’s economic and social development with these goals, leveraging its strengths in finance and innovation to serve as a global connector. The seminar highlighted opportunities for Hong Kong in science, technology, and talent development, reinforcing its role in China’s modernization drive. [Note: The team will monitor the news closely for its development. It is expected the entire Plan will be publicly announced in Mar 2026.]

Topic: Mass Weekend Travel: 403,000 Hongkongers Head North
Points: On Nov 22, Hong Kong recorded 403,000 residents travelling to Chinese Mainland, marking the second-highest Saturday since October. Return traffic surged on Nov 23 (Sunday), causing severe congestion at Shenzhen Bay and Liantang checkpoints. | This was the sixth consecutive weekend exceeding 100,000 Mainland visitors to Hong Kong, underscoring robust cross-border mobility and leisure demand.

Topic: Macau Satellite Casino Closures Accelerates
Points: Satellite casino closure continues besides SJM and Casino Casa Real mentioned in last week, at least two locations will be also closing down: Casino Fortuna, one of the most profitable satellites under SJM’s license, will close on Dec 10, following an internal notice issued Nov 20. | Kam Pek Casino is expected to shut down on Nov 30, while Casino Ponte 16 will close on Nov 28 after SJM dropped plans for acquisition.

Topic: Macau Visitor Arrivals Surge in October
Points: Macau welcomed 3.47 million visitors in October, up 10.8% year-on-year, driven by Golden Week travel. In particular: Chinese Mainland: 2.54 million (+12%), with Individual Visit Scheme (IVS) travelers jumping 22.6% to 1.32 million. | Hong Kong visitors: 584,767 (-1%). | Macau recorded 33.14 million visitors YTD, up 14.1% YoY.

Topic: UK racing spared betting duty tax increase
Points: In the UK Autumn Budget on Nov 26, Chancellor Rachel Reeves confirmed the tax would remain at 15% (instead of rising to 21% as proposed in August), recognizing horse racing’s cultural and economic significance, while increasing taxes on other forms of online betting and gaming. | British Horseracing Authority (BHA), which led the “Axe The Racing Tax” campaign, welcomed the exemption, said this helps preserve vital revenue streams and protect around 85,000 jobs across the industry. It also added they will analyze the Budget in detail to identify any potential issues and looks forward to collaborating with the government to support the sport’s sustainable growth.

Topic: China-Japan Tensions Over Taiwan Remarks
Points: **Diplomatic tensions** continue following Prime Minister **Takaichi’s** remarks on **Taiwan**. | **China** warned of “severe countermeasures” unless **Takaichi** retracts her comments. | High-level talks failed to ease tensions. | **China’s travel advisory** is already affecting **Japan’s tourism sector**. | Hotel bookings, airline tickets, and group tours are being widely canceled. | **Chinese tourists**—who account for **23%** of foreign visitors and contributed over **¥1.64 trillion** in spending—are projected to decline by **25%**. | An additional **¥290 billion** loss is expected from reduced **Hong Kong** travelers. | Agencies report a **20%** drop in **Japan** tour inquiries, with cancellations driven by “psychological factors”

Topic: Rare Earth Trade Tensions Ease
Points: **China’s** suspension of expanded **rare earth export controls** has opened a window for improved relations with both the **United States** and the **European Union**, easing geopolitical tensions and stabilizing **global supply chains** for critical minerals. | **US–China**: **Chinese exports** of **rare earth permanent magnets** to the **US** surged **56.1%** in October to a nine-month high. | **EU–China**: While **EU** imports of **Chinese magnets** fell **16.3%** in October, **EU Ambassador Jorge Toledo** welcomed **China’s** policy pause as a chance to “build on stability” and restart dialogue. | Both sides reaffirmed commitments to improve export control coordination.

Topic: 15th National Games Evolution
Points: The **15th National Games**, held across the **Greater Bay Area**, mark a milestone in **China’s** ascent as a global sports powerhouse. | Featuring **419 gold medal events** across **34 sports**, the Games mirror **Olympic standards** and embody national unity, innovation, and ambition. | **Elite Development & Global Competitiveness**: A growing emphasis on sporting excellence over provincial rivalry reflects **China’s** maturing athletic system. | **Innovation & Sustainability**: **AI-assisted officiating**, **robotic security**, **5G+8K livestreams**, and **100% renewable energy** power venues designed for both elite competition and public use. | **Mass Participation & Regional Integration**: With over **16,000 amateur athletes**, the Games celebrate grassroots engagement. | Cross-border events like the marathon and cycling race highlight the **“one country, two systems”** framework in action.

Topic: Property Market Growth Drag
Points: Former finance minister **Lou Jiwei** warned that **China’s property market downturn** has yet to bottom out and will continue to weigh on economic growth. | While real estate may not pose systemic risk its transformation could take up to **five years**. | Official data shows **fixed-asset investment** fell **1.7% YoY** in the first 10 months of **2025**, reflecting weak real estate and infrastructure activity.

Topic: HK GDP Forecast Upgrade 2025
Points: The **Hong Kong government** has revised its **2025 GDP growth forecast** from **2–3%** to **3.2%**, citing stronger-than-expected performance in the first three quarters and easing **US-China trade tensions**. | **Q3 growth** reached **3.8%**, driven by: **Strong export growth** to Asian markets | **Inbound tourism** up **11.9% YoY** (**Jan–Sep**), with **36.47 million visitors** | Positive asset market sentiment following **US interest rate cuts** | Robust financial activity, including **IPO momentum** and capital inflows | Government support for **innovation** and **AI adoption**.

Topic: Record National Games Performance
Points: **Cheng King-leung**, chairman of **Hong Kong’s National Games delegation**, praised the SAR’s **unprecedented success** at the ongoing competition. | **Cheng** credited the achievement to both athlete dedication and strong home crowd support. | While acknowledging **IOC Honorary President Thomas Bach’s** remarks on the **Greater Bay Area’s Olympic potential**, **Cheng** noted that any bid would be a national decision, though **Hong Kong** is well-equipped to host international events.

Topic: Galaxy Streamlines Baccarat Side Bets
Points: **Galaxy Entertainment Group** has joined other **Macau** casino operators in simplifying **side bet offerings** on its mass-floor and high-limit **baccarat tables** to enhance player engagement through simplified, high-payout formats. | This aligns with a broader market trend seen since August, with **Wynn Macau**, **MGM China**, **Melco Resorts**, and **SJM Holdings** also adopting pared-down side bet layouts.

Topic: Macau 2026 Casino GGR Forecast
Points: The **Macau government** projects **gross gaming revenue (GGR)** of **MOP236 billion** in **2026**, a **3.5% increase** over its revised **2025** forecast. | The estimate reflects recent momentum, with monthly **GGR** surpassing **MOP20 billion** from May to August, supported by strong tourism (**Sep**: **Chinese Mainland visitors** **+14.1% YoY**; **Hong Kong visitors** **-3% YoY**).

Topic: Q3 Casino Operator Performance
Points: All **casino operators** reported year-on-year growth of **1.5% to 20%**, except **SJM**, whose net revenue fell **6.2%**. | In November, **SJM** ceased or will cease operations at its satellite casinos: **Casino Legend Palace**, **Casino Casa Real**, and **Ponte 16**.

Topic: China-Japan Tensions Over Taiwan Remarks
Points: Diplomatic tensions continue following Prime Minister Takaichi’s remarks on Taiwan. China warned of “**severe countermeasures**” unless Takaichi retracts her comments. High-level talks failed to ease tensions. | China’s travel advisory is already affecting Japan’s tourism sector. Hotel bookings, airline tickets, and group tours are being widely canceled. Chinese tourists—who account for **23% of foreign visitors** and contributed over **¥1.64 trillion in spending**—are projected to decline by **25%**. | An additional **¥290 billion loss** is expected from reduced Hong Kong travelers. Agencies report a **20% drop in Japan tour inquiries**, with cancellations driven by “psychological factors”.

Topic: Rare Earth Trade Tensions Ease as China Recalibrates Export Strategy
Points: China’s suspension of expanded rare earth export controls has opened a window for improved relations with both the United States and the European Union, easing geopolitical tensions and stabilizing global supply chains for critical minerals.

Topic: U.S. Government Shutdown Ends
Points: President Donald Trump signed legislation on 12 November 2025, ending the longest government shutdown in U.S. history at **43 days (Oct 1–Nov 12)**. The bill, passed by the House (**222–209**) and approved by the Senate, funds operations through 30 January 2026, ensures backpay for federal workers, and aims to restart stalled programs—though recovery may take time amid continued partisan debate.

Topic: US-China Trade Pressures Ease with Tariff Rollbacks
Points: Following a presidential meeting, both countries rolled back key tariffs and export restrictions, offering temporary relief to global supply chains. Notable measures include: U.S. reducing fentanyl-related tariffs on Chinese goods from **20% to 10%**. China lifting restrictions on critical minerals, rare earths, and chemicals effective 10 November 2025. These steps benefit maritime and tech sectors, though deeper tensions remain.

Topic: 15th National Games Reflect China’s Sporting Evolution and Future Vision
Points: Xi declares National Games open. President Xi Jinping declared the 15th National Games open on November 9th, marking the first time the country's premier multi-sport event has been jointly hosted by Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao. Xi emphasized the Games’ role in: Strengthening China’s position as a global sports leader. Driving economic growth through sports. Advancing GBA integration through technology, infrastructure, and regulation— the men's road cycling race (Zhuhai→Macao→Hong Kong→Zhuhai) exemplified this integration. It featured RFID (radio-frequency identification)-enabled “zero delay” customs clearance, joint meteorological monitoring, and sparked widespread regional pride. “**GBA has the right elements to host the Olympics**” - Thomas Bach. Former International Olympic Committee president Thomas Bach encouraged the GBA to bid for the 2036 Olympics, praising its readiness. The mascots win hearts across China. Originally designed as a Chinese white dolphin, the mascot unexpectedly went viral after netizens joked about its appearance and nicknamed it “**大灣雞**”. Youth performers in bulky costumes brought it to life with playful energy. The mascot racked up over **370 million views on Douyin**, nearly **80 million on RedNote**, trended on Weibo for several days, and became a top internet sensation.

Topic: China’s Growing Global Investments Spur Yuan Internationalisation Push
Points: As Chinese firms expand overseas with strong investment momentum, economist Xiang Songzuo predicts Beijing will introduce enabling measures to advance **yuan internationalisation** and ease cross-border flows, driven by business demand rather than policy alone. | Despite strict capital controls requiring approval for outbound direct investment, rising appetite for yuan assets and swap agreements may prompt gradual facilitation to support global expansion without aggressive outflows.

Topic: China’s Property Market Remains a Drag on Growth
Points: Former finance minister Lou Jiwei warned that China’s property market downturn has yet to bottom out and will continue to weigh on economic growth. While real estate may not pose systemic risk, its transformation could take up to **five years**. Official data shows fixed-asset investment fell **1.7% YoY** in the first 10 months of 2025, reflecting weak real estate and infrastructure activity.

Topic: China's Fiscal Pivot: Tax Reform in 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030)
Points: Beijing proposes optimizing tax policies by boosting direct and local levies, tightening preferential incentives, and expanding to new sectors like strategic emerging industries and digital economy to enhance fiscal sustainability amid slowing traditional tax bases (e.g., VAT down 3.4% to **17.5 trillion yuan in 2024**) and rising outlays for consumption, investment, and livelihoods. | The plan balances revenue growth with an appropriate macro tax burden, addressing local governments' pressures from dwindling land sales and property downturns while funding public services without excessive business burdens.

Topic: 15th National Games
Points: National Games giving Hong Kong restaurants, retailers early business boost. Footfall Surge: Shopping centres near competition venues, like Kai Tak Sports Park, have already seen up to **20% weekday footfall increases**. Spending Momentum: Retailers and restaurant operators anticipate a **10% YoY boost** in business. Visitor Influx: With Hong Kong hosting eight events as part of the National Games, authorities expect around **100,000 visitors**. | Passion over paychecks, Hong Kong's handball heroes make history. Hong Kong’s men’s handball team placed **fourth** at the 2025 National Games—their best-ever result. Sixteen amateur players trained full-time despite limited resources, earning widespread support and emotional fanfare. Officials hope the breakthrough sparks greater recognition and backing for the sport’s future.

Topic: FEI General Assembly 2025 Successfully Concludes in Hong Kong
Points: The Fédération Équestre Internationale (FEI) wrapped up its 2025 General Assembly in Hong Kong on 7 Nov hosted by HKJC, drawing **267 delegates from 73 federations** after 27 years, and fostering global discussions on equestrian sport's future. | Key announcement: **Digital Horse Passport** (also known as Equipass), a collaborative initiative with the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) set for phased rollout starting in 2026 to integrate ID, health records, vaccinations, travel, and biosecurity for enhanced efficiency and welfare. | Gala awarded FEI Inspire to Shanghai's Beat as One – Stable Management Challenge for advancing horse welfare education in China underscoring regional collaborations and Hong Kong's growing prominence in equine development.

Topic: HKMA Launches Pilot for Real-Value Tokenised Money and Assets
Points: HKMA initiated real-value transactions using tokenised deposits and digital assets under Project Ensemble sandbox from November 14, 2025, involving **7 banks and 13 participants** for faster, transparent settlement through 2026, focusing on tokenised money-market funds and real-time liquidity. | HSBC completed **HK$3.8m (US$489,000)** cross-bank transfer for Ant International; aligns with sixfold surge in corporate tokenisation demand, positioning Hong Kong as global fintech hub.

Topic: Hong Kong IPO Market to Stay Hot in 2026: CICC
Points: CICC forecasts vibrant HK IPO market in 2026, driven by high-end manufacturing and tech firms (e.g., robotics), with over **100 IPOs in pipeline** despite mainland A-share bull run; HK raised **HK$216bn (US$27.8bn)** in first 10 months 2025. | Mainland fundraising up to **90bn yuan (US$12.6bn)** this year, but regulators' caution keeps HK attractive for global investors and valuation flexibility.

Topic: Returning Expats Fuel Hong Kong Luxury Rental Rebound
Points: Savills predicts **3-5% rise in luxury residential rents in 2026**, driven by returning Western expats (from Singapore, Europe, India), local professionals, and mainland Chinese via talent schemes; deals to exceed **660 in 2025** amid supply tightening from renovations. | Aligns with record **1.5m local companies** and **15k+ non-HK firms** registered (US/Europe active); cautiously positive outlook for property market.

Topic: A One-Year Truce on Tariffs with the US Was Confirmed
Points: The one-year Sino-US trade truce has brought relief and stability to Hong Kong exporters, allowing businesses to plan with more confidence. Industry leaders welcome the pause but remain cautious, noting unresolved geopolitical issues and the need for market diversification.

Topic: US Off-Year Elections
Points: The 2025 off-year elections held on November 4th resulted in significant Democratic victories in key state and city races, which are widely seen as the first major electoral test of President Donald Trump's second term. Virginia: Abigail Spanberger became the state’s first female governor, flipping control from Republican Glenn Youngkin. New Jersey: Mikie Sherrill secured a third straight Democratic term. New York City: Zohran Kwame Mamdani elected mayor—the city’s first Muslim, South Asian, and African-born leader. California: Voters passed Proposition 50, enabling the Democratic-led legislature to redraw congressional maps for 2026.

Topic: China’s Economy Expected to Slow as Exports Weaken
Points: October exports forecast to grow only **2.7%**, a sharp slowdown from September. Industrial production and retail sales also expected to decelerate.

Topic: Xi Urges Five-Point APEC Push for Regional Community
Points: At the 32nd APEC Economic summit, President Xi called for inclusive globalization through five key actions: Safeguarding multilateral trade. Promoting open regional cooperation. Stabilizing supply chains. Advancing green and digital trade. Ensuring equitable development. China pledged openness and deeper engagement, while markets responded positively.

Topic: HK Economy Grows A 'Robust' 3.8pc in Q3
Points: Hong Kong’s economy grew **3.8% year-on-year in Q3 2025**, outperforming previous quarters. Growth was driven by strong exports (up **12.2%**), rising private consumption (up **2.1%**), and robust retail sales (up **5.9%** in September). Experts cited surging IPOs, tourism, and private investment as signs of renewed business confidence. The government expects continued momentum, though external risks like trade barriers remain a concern.

Topic: Hong Kong Stocks Rally on Wall Street Rebound
Points: Hong Kong stocks rose **1.2%** to **26,245** on November 6th, lifted by broad sector gains and improved global sentiment after strong U.S. payroll data and China’s economic outlook. Beijing’s suspension of some U.S. tariffs also boosted confidence.

Topic: Support Measures Welcomed
Points: The Hong Kong SAR Government welcomed new Chinese Mainland measures to boost high-level opening and development. Key initiatives include: Expanding the talent exit endorsement to more provinces and free trade zones, enhancing Hong Kong’s role as a talent hub. Facial recognition clearance will be introduced at major ports to streamline cross-boundary travel. Additional measures support innovation collaboration in the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong zone. Designate four more Hong Kong-linked ports under the 240-hour visa-free transit policy, reinforcing the city’s position as a global tourism and connectivity hub.

Topic: Xi-Trump Summit
Points: President Trump and President Xi met on October 30, 2025, in Busan, South Korea, during the APEC summit. The meeting focused on below key issues: Trade relations and tariff reductions. Export restrictions on rare earth metals. Illegal fentanyl trafficking. Agricultural imports (e.g., U.S. soybeans). Major Outcomes: Trade Truce: The U.S. agreed to ease certain tariffs; China committed to resuming large-scale imports of American farm products. Rare Earths: China will delay new export restrictions, ensuring continued supply of critical materials. Fentanyl Cooperation: China pledged to intensify efforts to curb illegal fentanyl exports. Positive Tone: Trump described the meeting as “amazing” and rated it a “**12 out of 10**”.

Topic: China October PMI Data
Points: Manufacturing PMI: Fell to **49.0**, down 0.8 points from September, indicating continued contraction in factory activity. Non-Manufacturing PMI: Rose slightly to **50.1**, entering expansion territory. Service Sector: Improved to **50.2**, with high-growth areas like rail, air transport, postal services, accommodation, culture, sports, and entertainment maintaining strong momentum above **60.0**.

Topic: Chinese Vice-Premier Vows Further Opening Up of Financial Sector
Points: Vice-Premier He Lifeng 何立峰 pledged continued “**high-level opening up**” of China’s financial sector, welcoming more foreign investment and long-term capital. Foreign institutions expressed optimism and commitment to expanding investment in China. Recent approvals include UBS, Mizuho, and BNP Paribas, part of China’s push to attract global financial players.

Topic: Beijing Vows to Support Hong Kong in Better Integrating into National Development
Points: Integration & Development: The central government pledged deeper integration of Hong Kong into national development, emphasizing cooperation in economy, trade, science, technology, and culture. Strategic Positioning: Hong Kong’s role as an international financial, trade, and innovation hub will be reinforced, alongside efforts to build a high-end talent base. Governance & Autonomy: Reaffirmed “**one country, two systems**” and support for law-based governance, while continuing the “patriots ruling Hong Kong” principle. Shift in Focus: Places less emphasis on national security and more on economic growth and innovation, reflecting restored stability. Policy Outlook: Experts expect preferential policies to attract talent and accelerate innovation.

Topic: Hong Kong Finance Chief Says Economy ‘Doing OK’ Ahead of GDP Announcement
Points: Rate Adjustment: Major banks in Hong Kong lowered prime lending rates, following the U.S. Federal Reserve’s rate cut. HKMA Action: The HKMA reduced its base rate to **4.25%**, aligning with the Fed due to the linked exchange rate system. Q3 Outlook: Financial Secretary Paul Chan said GDP is “doing OK,” with IPO activity showing strength, but warned of challenges in catering and construction sectors. Unemployment Rate: Jobless rate rose to **3.9% (Jul–Sep)**, the highest since 2022.

Topic: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) Wraps Phase 2 of e-HKD Pilot
Points: Pilot Scope: The HKMA released findings from **11 industry pilots** exploring retail use cases of the e-HKD, including tokenised asset settlement, programmable payments, and offline transactions. Key Insights: e-HKD and tokenised deposits offer cost-efficient, resilient, and programmable transactions. Public trust in Hong Kong’s banking system led to similar perceptions of both instruments. Policy Direction: HKMA will prioritize wholesale applications (e.g., interbank and cross-border trade settlements) over retail for now, citing e-HKD’s suitability for large-value, credit-risk-free transactions. Next Steps: A policy and technical foundation will be completed by mid-2026. Retail rollout will depend on market demand, global trends, and tech readiness. HKMA will publish common tokenisation standards to support future digital money adoption.

Topic: Global Economy in Flux, Prospects Remain Dim
Points: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) projects a slowing global economy, with growth expected to decelerate from **3.3% in 2024 to 3.2% in 2025**. The global environment is marked by greater protectionism and volatility, though some extreme tariff measures have been tempered by recent deals.

Topic: Ongoing US Government Shutdown
Points: The federal government shutdown, which began on October 1, 2025, has now entered its fourth week. The shutdown has led to the furlough of approximately **900k federal employees** and continues to affect various government services.

Topic: US-China Trade War Xi-Trump Meeting
Points: US President Donald Trump will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping on October 30 in South Korea, the White House confirmed. Trump has stated he will prioritize confronting China on the fentanyl crisis and will also raise trade issues important to U.S. farmers. Analysts warn that the meeting is unlikely to yield major breakthroughs, as both sides dangerously believe they have “escalation dominance” and the upper hand.

Topic: The 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) Takes Shape
Points: A key Party meeting concluded this week, finalizing the recommendations for China's next Five-Year Plan. While the final plan will be formally approved in March 2026, the communique outlines key strategic pillars: Economic & Industrial Modernization - Build a modern industrial system; strengthen the real economy and manufacturing base; transition to advanced manufacturing; develop a robust domestic market, leveraging China's **400-million-strong middle-income group** to boost consumption. Technology & Innovation - Achieve technological self-reliance; make breakthroughs in science and technology; drive growth through “**new quality productive forces**” like generative AI and new energy vehicles. Green Development - Promote green development and the “Beautiful China Initiative”; support the green and low-carbon transformation of the economy. Social Welfare & Security - Improve public wellbeing and people's livelihoods; ensure employment; strengthen the national security system and capacity. Global Engagement - Expand external cooperation through trade and investment; promote high-standard opening up; remain a global anchor of stability and growth.

Topic: Implications of the 15th Five-Year Plan
Points: Hong Kong will proactively align with China’s upcoming 15th Five-Year Plan by identifying its strategic role within the national development blueprint. Experts noted that in light of global tensions, Hong Kong is expected to support mainland enterprises in going global and strengthen its role in financing China’s technological advancement.

Topic: Rising Jobless Rate
Points: Hong Kong's latest labour force statistics show a seasonally adjusted unemployment rate of **3.9%** for the July-September 2025 period, a rise of 0.2 percentage points. The increase was more distinct in sectors like social work activities and construction.

Topic: U.S. Government Shutdown Continues
Points: The U.S. federal shutdown, ongoing since September 30, entered its third week as the Senate failed to pass a House funding bill, delaying key data releases (e.g., inflation, jobs).

Topic: US-China Trade War Escalates with Multiple Measures
Points: President Trump threatened to halt Chinese cooking oil imports, and impose **100% tariffs on all Chinese goods** by November, alongside software export controls, port fee hikes, and student visa curbs; China retaliated with rare earth restrictions and port fees on U.S.-linked vessels (≥25% U.S. equity), risking TikTok deal disruptions, dipping the S&P 500, and boosting Bunge/ADM stocks.

Topic: China’s Retaliatory Measures to U.S. Trade Actions
Points: China responded to U.S. trade moves with port fees on U.S.-linked vessels (exempting 36% of global fleet built in China), sanctions on five U.S.-based subsidiaries of Hanwha Ocean, and tightened rare earth export controls, emphasizing tech self-reliance (AI, semiconductors) and diversified trade partnerships ahead of Trump-Xi talks.

Topic: Guangdong-HK Cross-Border Scheme Launched
Points: A new program allows Guangdong drivers a **3-day Hong Kong stay with 100 daily booking quotas**, starting next month, to boost tourism and economic ties.

Topic: NBA Eyes WNBA Game in China
Points: NBA Commissioner Adam Silver indicated a potential WNBA game in China “very soon”, aiming to grow basketball’s market and talent pipeline.

Topic: HKIMR Conference Highlights Trade Resilience
Points: The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research hosted its 14th Annual International Conference on the Chinese Economy (Oct 14) emphasized China’s stable **15% global export share** and diversification into emerging markets, addressing digital trade, innovative finance (e.g., Project mBridge), and green tech opportunities amid US-China trade tensions and supply chain shifts.

Topic: Hong Kong Stocks Rebound After Longest Losing Streak Since 2024
Points: The Hang Seng Index rose **1.2%**, ending a seven-day losing streak that had been fueled by global risk aversion and local property sector concerns, driven by U.S. Federal Reserve may cut rate sooner than expected that hopes easing Hong Kong’s currency peg pressure.

Topic: National Games Preparations Advance
Points: Chief Executive John Lee presented flags to Hong Kong’s National Games team, with cash incentives (up to **HK$1.5M**) for winners and a co-hosted event with Guangdong and Macau set for 2025.

Topic: Tourism Recovery Gains Momentum
Points: Hong Kong welcomed **36 million tourists in Q1-Q3 2025 (up 12% year-on-year)**, with Royal Caribbean increasing sailings and the National Games torch relay expecting **100,000+ visitors** and **4,000 athletes/media**.

Topic: NBA Games and Concerts Drive Tourism Surge
Points: The NBA China Games and concerts pushed Macau’s hotel occupancy to **90%**, bolstering tourism recovery and economic activity.

Topic: New Maritime Rules as Trade Countermeasure
Points: In a direct response to new U.S. port fees targeting China-linked vessels, the Chinese government updated its international maritime transport regulations, granting itself the authority to impose special port fees or block ships from entering Chinese ports. The world's first scheduled China-Europe Arctic Express container service also launched, offering a faster alternative to traditional routes.

Topic: The U.S. Federal Government Shutdown Stretched Into Its Second Week
Points: The U.S. Federal Government Shutdown Stretched Into Its Second Week with No Resolution in Sight. Deepening Political Stalemate: The Senate failed for the sixth and seventh times to pass dueling funding bills from Republicans and Democrats, with no negotiations publicly underway. Uncertainty for Federal Workers: The White House suggested that **750,000 furloughed workers** are not guaranteed back pay, creating fear and uncertainty. Strains on Essential Services: A slight increase in air traffic controllers calling in sick, and the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.C., has closed its doors.

Topic: 2025 Golden Week
Points: The eight-day National Day-Mid-Autumn Festival holiday created a Super Golden Week in 2025 characterized by massive population movement and a clear shift towards more experiential consumption.

Topic: China’s Fourth Plenum 二十屆四中全會
Points: The upcoming Fourth Plenum of China’s Communist Party, scheduled for October 20–23, is expected to bring the highest turnover in the Central Committee in eight years, largely due to officials being sidelined amid corruption investigations.

Topic: 2025 Golden Week
Points: This year's National Day Golden Week holiday, led to notable increases in the number of visitors in Hong Kong — boosting local retail, catering and hospitality sectors, alongside record racecourse attendance and robust betting turnover.

Topic: Hong Kong Government's Directive on The Official English Translation for "中国内地"
Points: The Hong Kong SAR government has stipulated that the official English translation for 中国内地 must be **Chinese Mainland**  not the previously often used "Mainland China""

Topic: 2025 Golden Week
Points: The 2025 Golden Week in Macau set new tourism records, with the eight-day holiday bringing in over **1.14 million visitors**.

Topic: NBA China Games
Points: The NBA is holding its first games in China since 2019, with the Phoenix Suns and Brooklyn Nets playing two preseason matches at The Venetian Arena in Macao on October 10 and 12, 2025. The event marks a significant return for the league after a six-year hiatus caused by a political firestorm, re-establishing its presence in its most important overseas market. The games are expected to provide a boost to local tourism, with reports of visitors flocking into Macau for the event and tickets for the sold-out games seeing high demand.

Topic: China-India Direct Flights to Resume to Repair Ties
Points: China and India have finalised a schedule to resume direct flights, with the first trips set to restart later this month as both countries cautiously ease bilateral tensions amid increasingly turbulent geopolitical headwinds. The resumption of direct flights would end a five-year suspension between the world’s two most populous countries. India and China initially agreed to resume direct flights in January and reaffirmed the decision in June, while India lifted restrictions on tourist visas for Chinese nationals earlier this year.

Topic: Trump Eyes Firing Thousands of Federal Workers Over Shutdown
Points: The US federal government shut down since Wednesday morning after a deadlocked Congress failed to reach a funding deal. President Donald Trump is weighing slashing “thousands” of federal jobs ahead of a meeting with his budget director, Russell Vought, as the White House looks to ratchet up pressure on Democrats to end the government shutdown. White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt told reporters on Thursday, saying that the “entire team at the White House” was working to identify possible cuts.

Topic: China Announces Date for Key Meeting to Discuss Next 5-Year Plan
Points: The Communist Party of China will hold its annual conclave between October 20 and 23 in Beijing to discuss the next five-year plan, a blueprint that will set out the country’s economic, political and social goals as it grapples with challenges from the United States. The 14th five-year plan is now in its final year. Under the rules, the 15th plan covering 2026-2030 must be endorsed by a plenary session of the party, after which it will be submitted to the annual legislative session in March for final endorsement.

Topic: Golden Start to the Golden Week for Hong Kong Businesses
Points: The tourism and retail sectors are celebrating a vibrant start to the eight-day National Day Golden Week holiday, welcoming over **224,000 mainland visitors** by 9pm on the first day (Oct 1) – a five percent increase from last year. Over **200 tour groups** arrived on the first day of the Golden Week, with a projected total of **1,200** for the entire holiday. While visitors come from various backgrounds, it is anticipated long-haul travelers from Hunan, Hubei, and southern regions will stay in the city for one to two nights, boosting local spending.

Topic: Hong Kong Marks National Day with Fireworks, Naval Ship Tours and Horse Races
Points: Hundreds of thousands of spectators packed Hong Kong’s harbourfront for a fireworks display on National Day, while others flocked to Sai Kung reservoir and Sha Tin Racecourse. The Hong Kong Jockey Club said more than **13,000 mainlanders** visited the Sha Tin Racecourse for the National Day Cup, a record. They accounted for nearly **40 per cent** of the total turnout of **34,000**, which was 1.52-fold higher than a year ago.

Topic: Hong Kong to Begin Nomination Period for Legislative Election on Oct 24
Points: Hong Kong will begin its two-week nomination period for the next Legislative Council election on October 24 in only the second poll held under Beijing’s “**patriots-only**” electoral reform. The nomination period would run until November 6 and called on hopefuls vying for the **90 seats** to submit their forms as early as possible in case any errors need to be corrected. Under the new system, the legislature has been expanded to 90 members, with only **20 directly elected** from geographical constituencies. Another **30 are returned from trade-based functional constituencies**, while **40 are chosen by the powerful Electoral Committee**, which is dominated by Beijing loyalists.

Topic: Retail Sales Grow at Fastest Pace in 20 Months
Points: Retail sales grew at their fastest pace in 20 months in August, jumping **3.8 percent year on year**. The Census and Statistics Department estimated the value of total retail sales at **HK$30.3 billion**, which was higher than the revised HK$29.67 billion of sales registered in July. The latest pace of growth was the fastest since December 2023.

Topic: NBA China Games
Points: The NBA is holding its first games in China since 2019, with the Phoenix Suns and Brooklyn Nets playing two preseason matches at The Venetian Arena in Macao on October 10 and 12, 2025. The event marks a significant return for the league after a six-year hiatus caused by a political firestorm, re-establishing its presence in its most important overseas market. The games are expected to provide a boost to local tourism, with reports of visitors flocking into Macau for the event and tickets for the sold-out games seeing high demand.

Topic: EU is Preparing to Hit China with 20 New Anti-Dumping Probes
Points: The European Union is planning to sharply ramp up its trade defences against China in the coming weeks, as it looks to protect its industries from cut-price competition and industrial spillovers in the world’s second-largest economy, a former top official has said. Former trade commissioner Cecilia Malmstrom said there were “preparations for another **20 anti-dumping investigations** in a variety of fields going on”.

Topic: Trump Plans New Tariff Push on Pharmaceuticals, Heavy Trucks and Furniture
Points: President Donald Trump announced a fresh round of tariffs on pharmaceuticals, heavy trucks and furniture, including a **100% duty on patented drugs** unless the producer is building a manufacturing plant in the US. The new industry-focused tariffs are set to begin next Wednesday.

Topic: US and Chinese Officials Agree to Step Up Communications
Points: Senior officials from the United States and China agreed to step up communications to help manage their differences following a meeting in New York on Sep 25. The meeting marks a latest step to stabilise relations ahead of a possible meeting between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump.

Topic: Hong Kong Home Prices Rise Slightly While Rents Near Historic Peak
Points: Hong Kong’s lived-in home prices rose by **0.14 per cent in August**, suggesting a gradual recovery in the city’s struggling residential property market. Hong Kong’s residential rents also climbed in August, nearing a record high. The rental index jumped by **1.12 per cent** – the largest increment in 14 months – to **198.7**, just 1.4 points shy of the peak of 200.1 recorded in August 2019.

Topic: Hong Kong’s Exports Rise Amid Extended Trade Truce
Points: Hong Kong’s exports rose by **14.5 per cent in August** year on year to **HK$436.6 billion**, amid a Sino-US trade truce and a surprise rebound in shipments to America and Europe, alongside continued solid demand in Asia, which helped offset wider economic uncertainties. The year-on-year increase marked an uptick from the **14.3 per cent** recorded in July and the **11.9 per cent** logged in June.

Topic: Casinos Reopen After 33-Hour Shutdown Amid Typhoon
Points: Macau casinos were forced to shutter for **33 hours** by the strongest tropical cyclone of the year, with all their gambling operations having resumed at 2:00 am on Sep. The reopening time was announced in the official gazette on Thursday, signed off by the chief executive.

Topic: Over 20 Macau Luxury Hotels Flag Sold Out for Oct Golden Week
Points: Over **20 luxury hotels in Macau** – all housed within casino resort complexes – appear to have sold out their rooms for at least five nights of the upcoming eight-day October Golden Week holiday.

Topic: Fed Approved Quarter-Point Interest Rate Cut
Points: The Federal Reserve on Sep 17 approved a widely anticipated rate cut and signaled that two more are on the way before the end of the year as concerns intensified over the U.S. labor market even as inflation is still in the air. The Federal Open Market Committee lowered its benchmark overnight lending rate by a quarter percentage point. The decision puts the overnight funds rate in a range between **4.00%-4.25%**.

Topic: Trump Hinted at the Possible Extension of a Trade Truce with China
Points: US President Donald Trump on Sep 18 hinted at the possible extension of a trade truce with China and at facilitating a deal for TikTok’s continued operation in America, as the market eagerly awaits any signs of progress in an anticipated phone call between the two countries’ leaders today. Trump said: “We’re pretty close to a deal. We may do an extension with China, but it’s an extension based on the same terms that we have right now, which are pretty good terms.”

Topic: China’s Offshore Yuan Strengthens Further
Points: Ahead of an anticipated interest rate cut from the US Federal Reserve this week, the offshore yuan strengthened past a rate of **7.1 against the US dollar** for the first time in nearly a year – another milestone reached in a gradual shift of China's monetary policy that has seen the currency gain ground over the last month. On Sep 17 morning, the offshore yuan reached **7.0999 per US dollar**, its strongest showing since November.

Topic: China’s Youth Unemployment Soars to 2-Year High
Points: China’s urban youth unemployment rate rose last month to the highest level since the data set was adjusted, as career prospects for young people have weakened amid an economic slowdown. The jobless rate for those aged 16 to 24, excluding students, rose to **18.9 per cent in August** from 17.8 per cent in July.

Topic: Hong Kong Expects 1.5m Mainland Tourists During National Day Golden Week
Points: The Travel Industry Council of Hong Kong expects **1.5 million mainland visitors** to arrive in Hong Kong during the National Day Golden Week, representing an estimated **10 percent increase** compared to last year. Approximately **3 percent** of these visitors, around **45,000 individuals**, will arrive through roughly **1,300 tour groups**, a year-on-year increase of nearly 10 percent.

Topic: Hong Kong Sticking With 2-3% Growth Target Despite Rate Cut
Points: Hong Kong’s finance chief has maintained his forecast of economic growth of between **2 and 3 per cent** this year, citing a volatile external environment despite a base interest rate cut by the Monetary Authority. “Even with the interest rate cut, there are still too many significant external variables which we cannot control, such as the development of tariffs and how far the United States’ protectionism goes,” Financial Secretary Chan Mo-po said.

Topic: Policy Address 2025 Revealed Efforts in Economic Reforms
Points: Hong Kong’s leader has delivered a comprehensive policy blueprint on Sep 17, pushing for further economic reforms by expediting key infrastructure projects and doubling down on the city’s competitive strengths, while also improving livelihoods, notably charting more paths to home ownership. Chief Executive John Lee Ka-chiu vowed to entice more high value-added industries and enterprises to the city by offering preferential policy packages. For the first time, he also floated the idea of settling government expenditure in **renminbi**.

Topic: Bullish Sentiment in US Stocks Amid Elevated Risks
Points: Stocks hovered near record highs at the start of the week, with investors anticipating an interest-rate cut in the Federal Reserve’s upcoming policy meeting. The **MSCI All Country World Index** held steady after closing at an all-time high on Sep 12. However, even the most optimistic investors are aware of potential problems that could halt the market's rise. With stock prices at some of the highest levels this century, the main risks include issues with artificial intelligence trends, damage from **President Donald Trump**’s trade policies, growing government debt, and a weakening job market.

Topic: Trump Expects Big Cut From Federal Reserve
Points: **President Donald Trump** predicted a “big cut” from the Federal Reserve this week ahead of a pivotal meeting at which the central bank’s governors are expected to ease policy for the first time in nine months. The Fed is widely expected to cut interest rates on Sep 17 as it grapples with a slowing labor market, stubborn inflation and an unprecedented push by **Trump** for lower borrowing costs. The median forecast from a Bloomberg survey of economists is for a **25 basis-point reduction**.

Topic: China Missed Retail Sales and Industrial Output Forecasts in August
Points: China’s economy showed signs of strain in August, as sluggish domestic demand, headwinds from the US trade war and a prolonged property downturn continued to weigh on several major indicators. Production at Chinese factories and mines expanded **5.2%** last month from a year earlier, compared with July’s gain of **5.7%**. The median forecast of economists in a Bloomberg survey was for an increase of **5.6%**. Meanwhile, retail sales grew **3.4%** on year in August, slower than an expectation for an increase of **3.8%** and down from **3.7%** in the previous month.

Topic: Hong Kong Legalizes Basketball Betting
Points: The Legislative Council of Hong Kong On Thursday passed the third reading of the Betting Duty (Amendment) Bill 2025, which will legalize basketball betting. The Hong Kong Government will follow the existing model for horse racing and football betting by issuing a basketball betting license to **Hong Kong Jockey Club**, subject to stipulated conditions. Betting tax calculation will mirror the current football betting rate with **50%** of net profit to be levied as betting tax.

Topic: Rising Interbank Rates and Stronger Hong Kong Dollar
Points: Hong Kong dollar interbank rates rose across the board. The one-month **HIBOR**, tied to mortgage rates, rose for two straight days, gaining **2.84 basis points** to **3.19036%** as of 11:15 AM on Sep 15, the highest since August 29’s **3.29655%**. Bloomberg data shows the **Hong Kong dollar** strengthened by up to **51 basis points** to **7.774** at the same time on Sep 15, its strongest level since May 9’s **7.7689%**.

Topic: Putin and Kim Join Xi at Landmark Military Parade
Points: China hosted two dozen world leaders, including **Vladimir Putin** and **Kim Jong-un**, for a huge military parade in Tiananmen Square on Sep 3 to mark the 80th anniversary of the end of World War II. The event marked the first public appearance together for the three leaders, signaling their willingness to coordinate in challenging the US-led global order, with **Xi** stating the Chinese nation is determined to stand self-reliant and strong.

Topic: Rally in Gold on Rising Demand and Looming Fed Rate Cut
Points: Gold headed for a third weekly gain, ahead of a US jobs report that may reinforce bets that the Federal Reserve will cut interest rates later this month. Bullion traded near **$3,550 an ounce**, having slipped from an all-time high of **$3,578.51 an ounce** reached on Sep 3.

Topic: US Appeals Court Rules Most Trump Tariffs Illegal
Points: A US appeals court has ruled that most tariffs issued by US President **Donald Trump** are illegal. In a 7-4 decision, the Court rejected **Trump**'s argument that the tariffs were permitted under an emergency economic powers act, calling them invalid as contrary to law.

Topic: China Stock and Yuan Rally Lift Investors’ Risk Appetite
Points: Confidence in China's A-share market has strengthened. The mainland stock benchmark **CSI 300 Index** has climbed over **10%** last month, while the **yuan** has risen about **1%** against the dollar. Meanwhile, Mainland traders’ leveraged bets hit a record **2.28 trillion yuan** in margin trades as of Sep 1, surpassing the 2015 peak of **2.27 trillion yuan**.

Topic: Hong Kong PMI Returns to Expansion
Points: S&P Global Hong Kong Purchasing Manager's Index - an indicator of local private sector - rose to **50.7 in August**, up from **49.2 in July**, marking a return to expansion territory for the first time in seven months and indicating a significant improvement in business conditions.

Topic: Hong Kong Retail Recovery Rolls on for Third Month
Points: A recent improvement in Hong Kong’s retail sector spilled into July, with sales rising by **1.8 per cent year on year** in a sign that the industry had stabilized. The increase marked the third month in a row of growth following 14 consecutive months of decline.

Topic: August Gaming Revenue Setting Post-Pandemic High
Points: Macau casinos raked in a total of **MOP22.16 billion** in gross gaming revenue (GGR) in August, representing a **12.2 per cent year-on-year increase**. Last month’s figure also sets a new post-pandemic high, surpassing the **MOP22.13 billion** in July.

Topic: Macau Faces Drop in Per Capita Spending from Mainland Visitors
Points: Data from the first half of 2025 shows that the average non-gambling expenditure per Mainland tourist was **1,970 yuan**, reflecting a year-on-year decrease of **12.8%**. **Ip Kuai Peng**, vice rector of the City University of Macau, highlighted that this decline is linked to the weak economic environment and evolving consumption habits. Notably, there has been a shift in spending patterns, with mainland tourists increasing their expenditure on dining and other areas while reducing their focus on shopping.

Topic: Macau Summer Visitors Up 7.4% from Pre-Pandemic Levels
Points: Macau recorded **7.68 million visitor arrivals** during July and August, averaging **123,000 arrivals per day**. This marked a **7.4 percent increase** compared to the same period in 2019, before the pandemic.

Topic: Trump Ordered Removal of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook
Points: US President **Donald Trump** has said he will immediately remove Federal Reserve official **Lisa Cook** from her position for alleged mortgage fraud.

Topic: US Threatened 200% Tariffs on China Over Rare Earth Magnets
Points: US President **Donald Trump** said on Aug 25 that China must ensure the US supply of rare earth magnets or face **200 per cent tariffs**, and that he will continue to allow Chinese students into the country. | The president also said that Chinese students can come to the US to pursue degrees. “I hear so many stories about we’re not going to allow their [Chinese] students … to come in. We’re going to allow their students to come in. It’s very important, **600,000 students**,” **Trump** said, which would more than double the current number of Chinese students learning in the country.

Topic: 9 Billiard Venues to Admit Children
Points: The Leisure and Cultural Services Department (LCSD) has approved applications from nine licensed billiard establishments to relax entry rules for youth, reducing the minimum age from 16 to **8** and extending the stay limit from 8pm to 11pm.

Topic: Chinese Traders Sell Record Amount of Hong Kong Stocks
Points: Investors in mainland China sold a record **HK$20.4 billion** worth of Hong Kong-listed stocks on Aug 28, a sign the country’s army of investors are returning to their local market amid a breakneck rally.

Topic: Government Updates M Mark System
Points: The government has announced new changes to the “**M**” Mark system to improve the quality, appeal, and economic impact of major events. Starting 16 September, all applications must be submitted at least six months before the event is held or announced. Funding for approved events will range from **$6m to $15m**, depending on the vetting outcome, meaning not every approved application will receive the maximum allocation.

Topic: Hong Kong Home Prices Log Fourth Straight Gain
Points: The index of secondary home prices gained **0.42 per cent month on month** to **387.9 in July**. It was the index’s highest level since **289.2 in December**, indicating the city’s residential property market may have turned a corner.

Topic: Hong Kong July Exports Value Rises
Points: The value of Hong Kong’s total exports of goods increased by **14.3 percent** over a year earlier to **HK$446.3 billion** in July, after a rise of **11.9 percent** in the previous month. For the first seven months of 2025 as a whole, the value of total exports of goods increased by **12.7 percent** year-on-year, while that of imports of goods rose by **13.2 percent**.

Topic: Potential Deal to End Ukraine-Russian War
Points: **President Donald Trump** and Russian President **Vladimir Putin** will meet in Anchorage, Alaska on Friday, with the U.S. president's hopes of sealing a ceasefire agreement on Ukraine.

Topic: China Economy Shows Signs of Strain
Points: China’s economy showed signs of strain in July, with several headline indicators losing momentum. | Retail sales, a major gauge of consumption, rose by **3.7 per cent year on year in July**, a drop in pace compared with the **4.8 per cent** growth rate recorded in June. | Industrial output grew by **5.7 per cent year on year in July**, down from **6.8 per cent** in June. | Property investment continued to decline, falling **12 per cent** in the period from January to July, compared with a **11.2 per cent** slump recorded in the first six months of the year.

Topic: China Sanctioned Two EU Banks
Points: China sanctioned **UAB Urbo Bankas** and **AB Mano Bankas** to retaliate after the European Union targeted some Chinese lenders over Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

Topic: Gradual Return of Tourists to Hong Kong
Points: The number of visitors to Hong Kong rose by **12 per cent year on year in July**, with long-haul arrivals from countries such as Britain, the United States and France showing the biggest increase at **21 per cent**. The cumulative total for the first seven months of the year was around **28 million**, also a **12 per cent** increase over the same period last year.

Topic: Likelihood of US-China Tariff Truce
Points: A 90-day extension of a US-China tariff truce is likely, US Commerce Secretary **Howard Lutnick** said on Aug 7, the most concrete signal from the US side about moving the deadline since bilateral talks concluded in Stockholm last week.

Topic: US Levy on Imported Chips
Points: President **Donald Trump** said the United States will impose a tariff of about **100%** on imports of semiconductors but offered up a big exemption - it will not apply to companies that are manufacturing in the U.S. or have committed to do so.

Topic: US Tariffs Took Effect
Points: US President **Donald Trump**'s sweeping new tariffs on more than 90 countries around the world have come into effect on Aug 7. The new levies raise the United States’ effective tariff rate above **17%**, the highest tax since the Great Depression.

Topic: China Exports Beating Market Forecasts
Points: China saw outbound shipments rise last month by **7.2 per cent**, year on year, to **US$321.8 billion**. This was higher than the **5.8 per cent** growth rate recorded in June. China’s exports continued to accelerate in July as a fall in shipments to the United States was offset by growth in a range of markets.

Topic: Hong Kong Possibility to Reverse Fiscal Deficits
Points: Financial Secretary **Paul Chan** on Aug 3 said that Hong Kong could reverse its expected fiscal deficit for this financial year, as the performance of the market in the first half of the year had been positive.

Topic: US Reciprocal Tariff Adjustments
Points: U.S. President **Donald Trump** signed an executive order on July 31 that modified “reciprocal” tariffs on dozens of countries, with updated duties ranging from **10% to 41%**. Tariffs on Canada took effect on Friday, August 1, 2025, increasing from **25% to 35%**, while other country-specific rates are set to apply from August 7, 2025, to address trade deficits and national security concerns.

Topic: US Transshipment Tariff Threat
Points: President **Donald Trump** has threatened to pile an additional **40% tariff** on any product that Washington determines to be “transshipped” through another country, a punishment aimed at stopping goods mainly from China dodging US duties.

Topic: China Robotics Industry Expansion
Points: China’s robotics sector is rapidly advancing, fueled by Beijing’s push to lead in emerging technologies amid U.S. tech rivalry. Leveraging vast manufacturing capacity, rapid innovation cycles, and robust supply chains, the industry is scaling to meet domestic demand and drive global adoption, with customizable robots gaining traction in industrial and service applications.

Topic: Hong Kong Football Festival
Points: The inaugural **Hong Kong Football Festival** concluded on July 31, 2025, attracting nearly **60,000 fans** to training sessions and **100,000 spectators** to matches featuring Liverpool, AC Milan, Arsenal, and Tottenham. The event set a new attendance record at Hong Kong’s newest stadium, with **49,975 attendees**, and generated an estimated economic impact of **HK$428 million**.

Topic: Hong Kong Retail Sales Up
Points: Retail sales rose **0.7% year-on-year in June** to a provisional **HK$30.1 billion**. However, after adjusting for inflation, the volume of retail sales fell by **0.3%** compared to the same month last year.

Topic: Hong Kong Stablecoin Regulatory Framework
Points: Hong Kong’s stablecoin ordinance, effective August 1, 2025, places cryptocurrencies under rigorous oversight akin to banking regulations. The **Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA)** has finalized licensing and anti-money laundering guidelines, with the first stablecoin licenses expected in early 2026. This prudent approach aims to foster sustainable digital asset growth, sparking significant interest among issuers.

Topic: Macau Record Casino Revenue
Points: Macau’s casino gross gaming revenue (GGR) for July 2025 reached **MOP22.13 billion**, the highest monthly figure since January 2020, reflecting a **19% year-on-year increase** and a **5% rise** from June’s **MOP21.06 billion**. This strong performance signals a robust recovery in the gaming sector post-pandemic.

Topic: US-Japan Trade Deal
Points: On July 23, 2025, the United States and Japan reached a trade deal where the U.S. agreed to impose a **15% tariff** on Japanese exports, down from a threatened **25%**, providing relief to Japanese automakers and other industries. Japan committed to investing **$550 billion in the U.S.** and opening its markets to American cars, trucks, rice, and other agricultural products.

Topic: China Rising Budget Deficit
Points: China’s budget deficit reached a record **5.25 trillion yuan** in the first half of 2025, a **45% increase** from the previous year, reflecting intensified government efforts to bolster domestic demand amid reduced exports to the U.S. due to tariffs imposed by **President Donald Trump**.

Topic: Hang Seng Index Performance
Points: **Hang Seng Index** closed at their highest since mid-November 2021 on Thursday, as investors cheered on an easing of China-US tensions. However, it fell **1.1%** on Jul 25, closing at **25,388**, ending a five-day **4.8% gain**.

Topic: HKJC Partnership with Xinjiang
Points: The **Hong Kong Jockey Club** has signed a five-year memorandum of understanding with the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region to support the development of a modern and internationally recognised horse industry in western China.

Topic: Hong Kong IPO Market Surge
Points: Hong Kong’s IPO market experienced a **sevenfold increase** in funds raised in the first half of 2025 compared to the same period in 2024, with eight A-share companies listed in Hong Kong raising over **HK$78 billion**.

Topic: Hong Kong Private Residential Property Price Rebound
Points: The **Centa-City Leading Index (CCL)** rose to **137.76 points**, up **0.97% week-on-week**, marking the largest weekly gain in 16 weeks. The CCL has surpassed the 137-point level, slightly above the year-end 2024 figure of **137.64 points**, fully recovering its 2025 losses.

Topic: Trump Announces Tariff Letters to 150 Countries
Points: President **Donald Trump** said he would send letters to more than **150 countries** notifying them their tariff rates could be **10% or 15%**.

Topic: US Passes Stablecoin Regulation Bill
Points: The U.S. House of Representatives on Thursday passed a bill to create a regulatory framework for U.S.-dollar-pegged cryptocurrency tokens known as stablecoins, sending the bill to President **Donald Trump**.

Topic: China Q2 Economy Grows 5.2%
Points: China’s economy expanded by **5.2 per cent in the second quarter**, keeping it broadly on track to meet this year’s growth target, but analysts cautioned that weak domestic demand and rising external uncertainties could provoke a slowdown in the second half of 2025.

Topic: HKJC 2024/25 Racing Season Performance
Points: The 2024/25 racing season wagering turnover rose **3%** to **HK$138.85 billion**, driven by optimized jackpots, larger field sizes, increased mainland and international tourism, and globalized racing through **HKJC**'s World Pool Strategy. Local races saw a record **HK$31.76 billion** in commingling turnover, up **10.1%** from last season. Racecourses attracted **1.7 million visitors**, including **195,786 mainland tourists**, a **110% increase** from 93,000 last season.

Topic: Hong Kong Unemployment Remains at 3.5%
Points: Hong Kong’s jobless rate remained at a 30-month high of **3.5 per cent** between April and June, with authorities warning of an ongoing uncertain external environment and worsening unemployment from more graduates entering the workforce. Preliminary data showed that the number of unemployed persons reached **136,200**, slightly higher than **135,800** in the previous three months.

Topic: Macau Strong Tourism Recovery
Points: Inbound visitation has recovered to about **95 per cent** of the 2019 level, with **19.22 million visitors** having made their way into Macau between January and June. For the first six months, the hotel occupancy rate rose by **5.8 percentage points** to **89.8 per cent**.

Topic: Trump Announces New Tariffs on Copper Brazil and Others
Points: On July 9, **Trump** confirmed a **50% tariff** on copper imports set to take effect on August 1. | On the same day, **Trump** announced a **50% tariff** on Brazil, along with varying rates on six smaller economies including the Philippines and Iraq, effective August 1. | On July 10, **Trump** announced a **35% tariff** on certain Canadian goods, set to take effect on August 1.

Topic: Trump Confirms August 1 Tariff Deadline
Points: **Trump** confirmed that the deadline for imposing increased tariffs on various trading partners will be **August 1**, with no further extensions.

Topic: xAI Releases Grok 4
Points: **Elon Musk**'s xAI launched **Grok 4** on July 10. This new iteration features advanced reasoning capabilities and is positioned as a leader in AI benchmarks, including Humanity's Last Exam — a test of high-level problem-solving. **Musk** also announced plans to integrate Grok into Tesla vehicles soon.

Topic: HIBOR Hits Two-Month High
Points: The property-linked **HIBOR** rose for the third consecutive day to **1.075%** on July 8, reaching a new high for about two months.

Topic: HKJC Plans Major Divestiture from US Assets
Points: **HKJC** is reportedly selling up to **US$1 billion** (HK$7.8 billion) in investments in **Blackstone Group** and other buyout firms, reducing its exposure to US assets amid escalating trade tensions since **President Donald Trump** took office.

Topic: HKJC Sports Betting Legalisation
Points: The Legislative Council's Committee on the Gambling Tax (Amendment) Bill 2025 held its first meeting on July 11. The Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs, **Mak Mei-kuen**, stated that, in the short term, no other sports appear to have issues severe enough to warrant the last resort of legal regulation.
Hashtags: HKJC-related, Basketball Betting, Betting Tax, Sports & Entertainment

Topic: Trump Reaches Vietnam Trade Deal
Points: **Trump** announced a trade agreement with Vietnam that imposes a **20% tariff** on imports, effective before a July 9 deadline. The deal aims to open Vietnam's markets to the US with zero tariffs on American exports, while goods transhipped through Vietnam will face a **40% tariff**.

Topic: Trump Sets August 1 Tariff Deadline
Points: **Trump** announced that his administration will send letters to trading partners on Jul 4, setting unilateral tariff rates that will take effect on **August 1**, ranging from **10% to 70%**. About 10 or 12 letters will be sent initially, with a July 9 deadline for countries to respond to avoid higher import duties.

Topic: US House Passes Trump Policy Bill
Points: The US House of Representatives passed a significant tax-and-spending bill, known as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, marking a major legislative victory for President **Trump**. This bill revamps government spending, locks in tax cuts from his first term, and jeopardizes various clean energy projects linked to China.

Topic: China Imposes Anti-Dumping Tariffs on European Cognac
Points: China has announced anti-dumping tariffs on European cognac, primarily produced in France, effective for the next five years, with margins ranging from **27.7% to 34.9%**. This decision coincides with Foreign Minister **Wang Yi**'s European tour aimed at resolving trade disputes and improving relations.

Topic: Hong Kong First-Half IPOs Soar Eightfold
Points: In the first half of 2025, Hong Kong's IPOs surged eightfold, raising **$13.5 billion** and reclaiming the top spot globally for capital raised. This resurgence is attributed to increased participation from international investors and strong post-listing performance, with average returns exceeding **30%**.

Topic: Hong Kong May Retail Sales End 14-Month Contraction
Points: Hong Kong's retail sales increased by **2.4% year-on-year in May**, marking the end of a 14-month slump, with total sales reaching **HK$31.3 billion**. The growth was driven by a surge in visitors during China's Labour Day holiday, significantly exceeding previous government estimates.

Topic: Hong Kong Property Sales Hit 7-Month High
Points: Hong Kong's property market saw a surge in activity, with overall deals rising by **13% in June**, reaching a seven-month high of **7,271 transactions** and residential sales exceeding **5,000 units** for the fourth consecutive month.

Topic: Macau June GGR Up 19% Year-on-Year
Points: Macau's gross gaming revenue (GGR) for June reached **$2.60 billion**, reflecting a **19% increase** compared to the previous year. This growth signals a continuing recovery in the gaming sector as tourism and visitor numbers improve.

Topic: China and US Finalise Breakthrough Trade Deal
Points: China and the United States have reached a breakthrough trade agreement following high-level negotiations in London. Under the deal, China will review and approve export applications for controlled items, while the US will lift a series of restrictive measures against China. | The agreement marks a significant step in easing tensions over strategic technologies and export controls, with both sides reaffirming their commitment to stable economic ties. This development is expected to reduce uncertainty for global markets and may positively influence Hong Kong’s trade and investment outlook.

Topic: Iran-Israel Ceasefire
Points: Iran and Israel agreed to maintain ceasefire, although deemed to be fragile, after the U.S. entered the Israel’s war with attacks against Iran. On Jun 24, the Nasdaq reached a record high close for the first time since February while Brent Crude dropped **6.1% to $67.13/barrel**.

Topic: HKJC Pledges HK$450M for National Games
Points: The **Hong Kong Jockey Club** has pledged **HK$450 million** to support the Hong Kong Competition Region in the upcoming National Games, National Games for Persons with Disabilities, and National Special Olympic Games. This funding will aid athlete development, venue enhancement, and community engagement, reinforcing the Club’s commitment to sports and social inclusion.

Topic: HKMA Currency Intervention
Points: The **HKMA** intervened in the currency market for the first time since 2023 by selling **US$1.2 billion** to buy Hong Kong dollars as the currency hit the weak end of its trading band at **HK$7.85**. This action aims to counteract currency arbitrage and is attributed to decreased demand for the local dollar influenced by various economic factors.

Topic: Hong Kong Home Prices Stay Flat
Points: Home prices in Hong Kong remained flat in May, rising just **0.04%** from April, as lower interest rates helped stabilise the market. The home price index stood at **286.9**, though still **6.2% lower year-on-year**, suggesting a cautious but steady outlook.

Topic: Macau Slot Concession Extension
Points: The Macau government has extended **Macau Slot Co Ltd**'s sports betting concession for one year, until June 5, 2026. Macau Slot is required to reduce its non-resident workforce by **35%** and work with the government to recruit and retain local talent.

Topic: Geopolitical Tensions and Economic Outlook
Points: The Israel-Iran conflict continues to pose risks to global stability. While financial markets have reacted moderately so far, escalation could disrupt energy supply chains and impact inflation and growth forecasts. | Central banks remain cautious. **S&P Global** forecasts indicate below-potential growth for 2025–26, with risks from both trade tensions and geopolitical instability. | The Federal Reserve hinted at a pause in rate hikes.

Topic: Basketball Betting Legalization Advances
Points: The Hong Kong Government gazetted the Betting Duty (Amendment) Bill 2025 today, proposing a regulatory framework for basketball betting. The bill includes a **50% duty** on the operators’ net stake receipts, mirroring the football betting regime. If enacted, the **Hong Kong Jockey Club** will be licensed to operate basketball betting, with conditions aimed at minimizing social harm, especially among youth. The bill will be introduced for first reading in LegCo on July 2.

Topic: HKJC Simulcast Programme Expansion
Points: The **HKJC** has received government approval to significantly expand its simulcast programme, increasing the number of overseas race meetings offered for betting from **37 to 70 annually**. This move is expected to enhance betting turnover and diversify racing content for Hong Kong punters.

Topic: Hong Kong May Visitor Arrivals Surge
Points: Hong Kong welcomed over **4 million visitors in May**, a **20 per cent year-on-year increase**. More than **3.1 million** of last month’s visitors were from mainland China, a **19 per cent** rise from last year.

Topic: US-China Trade Truce Framework Agreed
Points: After two days of negotiation in London, US and China officials announced on Jun 10 that they have agreed on a framework to implement a trade truce. US will set its tariffs at **55%** and ease restrictions for Chinese students in US colleges and universities, while China will set its tariffs at **10%** and ease restrictions on exports of rare earths for six months. | Meanwhile, **Trump** indicated plans to establish unilateral tariff rates within the next two weeks, ahead of a July 9 deadline to reinstate higher duties on various economies.

Topic: China Economy Outlook May 2025
Points: China's economy has managed to endure recent trade disruptions, bolstered by government fiscal stimulus and preemptive actions by exporters. However, domestic consumption appears to be further weakening, with retail sales growth in May estimated to have slipped below **5%**, as industrial production remains steady amid a deepening contraction in property investment.

Topic: Asian Cup Qualifier Success at Kai Tak Stadium
Points: With an attendance of over **42,500 football fans**, the Asian Cup qualifier held on Jun 10 was proven to be a huge success as the first international match hosted at the **Kai Tak Stadium**. **Vincent Cheng Wing-shun**, vice-chairman of the government’s Major Sports Events Committee, voiced his support on the idea of forming a separate committee focused on developing strategies to turn sports into an industry that could boost the economy by leveraging the new stadium, especially in engaging the business community.

Topic: Hong Kong Leads Global IPO Market
Points: Hong Kong has surged ahead in the global IPO market, with fundraising skyrocketing over **sevenfold year-on-year to HK$108.7 billion** in the first half of 2025, surpassing both Nasdaq and the New York Stock Exchange. The number of listings in the city during the period also rose by **33% year-on-year to about 40 deals**, making it the third busiest market globally by deal count.

Topic: Macau Satellite Casino Closures
Points: Three major gaming concessionaires in Macau, including **SJM Resorts**, **Melco Resorts** and **Galaxy Casino**, will close **11 satellite casinos** by December 31, affecting approximately **6,000 employees**. This decision follows the expiration of a three-year transition period under new legislation aimed at regulating the casino partnership model.

Topic: US Trade Deficit Contracts Sharply
Points: The U.S. trade deficit contracted by a record **55.5%** to **$61.6 billion** in April, the lowest level since September 2023. Imports decreased by the most on record as the front-running of goods ahead of tariffs ebbed, which could provide a lift to U.S. economic growth this quarter. | **President Donald Trump** and Chinese President **Xi Jinping** held their first phone call since the start of the trade war, discussing tariffs and potential visits to each other's countries. Trump said I think we're in very good shape with China and the trade deal.

Topic: China Establishes 10 New National Data Pilot Zones
Points: China will establish **10 new national data pilot zones** in Beijing, Zhejiang, Anhui and other regions to encourage local governments to spearhead efforts in nurturing data-related market entities and expanding the data market and unlock the potential of integrating the real economy with the digital economy.

Topic: Hong Kong Basketball Betting License Proposal
Points: Hong Kong authorities have proposed a **50% duty** on the operators’ net betting profits from basketball gambling, while a public consultation found that **94% of respondents supported** legalising such activities.

Topic: Hong Kong Dragon Boat Festival Visitor Arrivals
Points: Around **460,000 visitor arrivals** were recorded in Hong Kong during the three-day Dragon Boat Festival long weekend of the Chinese mainland (May 31 to June 2), representing a year-on-year increase of about **11 percent**. | The **Hong Kong Tourism Board** has begun discussions with various payment platforms about sharing tourism-related data with the government for analysis, according to Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism **Rosanna Law Shuk-pui**. The initiative is part of the Blueprint for Hong Kong's Tourism Industry 2.0, which aims to enhance data and market analysis by collaborating with payment platforms, service providers, and travel websites.

Topic: Hong Kong Maintains 2025 GDP Growth Forecast
Points: Financial Secretary **Paul Chan** said the Hong Kong economy expanded solidly in the first quarter, with GDP increasing by **3.1 percent year on year**. However, the government is maintaining its forecast for Hong Kong's GDP growth at **two to three percent** for the year amid a slight easing in international trade tensions.

Topic: US Ban on Chinese and Hong Kong Student Applications
Points: On May 22, the **Trump** administration escalated the tension with foreign countries further when US Homeland Security Secretary **Kristi Noem** issued a letter revoking **Harvard University**'s license to enroll foreign students. | On May 28, U.S. Secretary of State **Marco Rubio** announced that the U.S. will aggressively revoke visas for Chinese and Hong Kong students, targeting those with ties to the Chinese Communist Party or studying in critical fields like STEM. The policy also includes enhanced scrutiny of future visa applications from China and Hong Kong, escalating U.S.-China tensions.

Topic: US Tariffs Upheld by Appeals Court
Points: A U.S. federal appeals court has temporarily allowed **President Trump**’s tariffs on many countries to stay in place, pausing a lower court’s ruling that said he lacked the authority to impose them without Congressional approval.

Topic: Hong Kong New Labour Policy for Skilled Trades
Points: The Hong Kong government announced today (May 30) that, starting June 30, 2025, a new pathway will be introduced to allow overseas individuals to apply for work in eight critically scarce skilled trades. Applicants must be non-degree professionals meeting the qualifications listed in the Skilled Talent List and aged between 18 and 40. The Skilled Talent List includes eight skilled trades: advanced manufacturing technician, nurse, aircraft maintenance technician, local vessel maritime technician, IT technician, elevator/escalator technician, building information modeling coordinator, and electrical technician. | The age limit for non-local skilled workers seeking employment in Hong Kong has been raised from 35 to **40** years old.

Topic: Hong Kong Response to US Student Visa Ban
Points: Hong Kong’s Education Bureau urged local universities to attract students affected by the U.S. visa ban, with **HKUST** offering unconditional admissions and streamlined processes for Harvard’s international students, including those from Hong Kong and China.

Topic: Trump Revokes Harvard International Student Enrollment
Points: The **Trump** administration has revoked **Harvard**'s certification to enroll international students, citing legal noncompliance. This decision affects thousands of students, causing confusion and concern. **Harvard** has deemed the move unlawful and is working to support its international community amid fears of significant impacts on its academic mission.

Topic: Hong Kong Launches Nine New Tourism Projects
Points: Hong Kong has launched nine new tourism projects aimed at enhancing visitor experiences and revitalizing local neighborhoods. These projects, featuring prominent brands and scenic peaks, are designed to attract more tourists and stimulate economic growth, reflecting the city’s unique characteristics and cultural offerings.

Topic: Hong Kong Stocks Track Sixth Weekly Gain
Points: Hong Kong stocks are set for a sixth consecutive weekly gain, driven by optimism over easing US-China tensions and positive economic data. The **Hang Seng Index** saw a rise, with notable gains in Chinese pharmaceutical stocks following a strong market debut by **Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals**.

Topic: US-China Tariff Agreement Reached
Points: Under a temporary truce, the U.S. will reduce additional tariffs on Chinese imports from **145% to 30%** for the next three months, while Chinese duties on U.S. imports will decrease from **125% to 10%**. Additionally, China has agreed to lift export restrictions on rare earth minerals and magnets used in high-tech manufacturing. This development has contributed to an increase in Wall Street stocks, with the **S&P 500** reaching its highest level since early March.

Topic: HIBOR Drops for Sixth Straight Day
Points: Hong Kong’s mortgage-related interbank offered rate fell for the sixth consecutive day by **36 basis points** on May 13, reaching **1.566 percent**, as local liquidity continues to improve. With the lower cost of funding, it is expected to boost the city’s property market and economy.

Topic: HKJC Partners with XIX Entertainment
Points: A significant partnership between **HKJC** and **XIX** was announced on May 12. **HKJC** CEO described this collaboration as heralding an exciting new era for **HKJC**, aiming to position it as a global sports entertainment brand and showcase Hong Kong as a center for global exchange, connectivity, and tourism.

Topic: Hong Kong April Visitor Arrivals
Points: The **Hong Kong Tourism Board** announced that the city welcomed approximately **3.8 million visitors in April**, marking a **13 percent increase** compared to the same period last year. Arrivals from Mainland, short-haul, and long-haul markets all showed double-digit year-on-year growth.

Topic: Hong Kong Banks Cut Headcounts
Points: On May 14, unexpected layoffs at **Hang Seng Bank** were reported, with some departments losing up to **20% of staff** and the hardest-hit team cut in half. Analysts attribute this to a challenging economic environment and weak retail/property sectors, a trend also observed with other bank layoffs in Hong Kong.
